..
Friday: A strong upper-level ridge responsible for the recent 
string of warm and dry weather will begin to slide east. As the
ridge axis shifts into Western Montana, southwest winds will 
increase aloft drawing warmer air into the region. High 
temperatures on Friday will warm another 5 degrees topping out 
in the upper 60s to lower 70s under sunny skies. Winds will 
remain light with a general easterly direction in the morning 
and slowly shift to the south in the afternoon. Speeds will 
remain below 10 mph except on the Palouse where easterly winds 
will be near 15 mph Friday morning. 

Saturday: A shortwave swings out of the Gulf of Alaska and across 
the Canadian border dragging a cold front through the Inland 
NW. Gusty westerly winds will develop across the region as 
pressure gradients tighten and afternoon mixing draws down 
25-35kts of winds aloft. The track of this system to the north 
is not ideal for strong enough winds for wind highlights but 
there will undoubtedly be the potential for some impacts. 
Anglers should be prepared for choppy lakes. Following a string 
of warm and dry weather, fuels remain unseasonably dry and the 
threat for swift fire spread in dry grasses will remain 
elevated, especially in the late afternoon as humidity levels 
drop between 25-30%. There will also be a threat for patchy 
blowing dust near recently worked fields on the Waterville 
Plateau and areas of the western and central Columbia Basin. 
Typically this time of year, dust sources are centered near 
recently plowed potato fields and where winter wheat has been 
planted. Ag reports suggests 70% of the winter wheat has emerged
which tends to lower the risk. Nonetheless, this is something 
that will need to be monitored closely. 

Winds will increase Saturday morning, peak mid afternoon and 
come down in the evening. Sustained speeds of 15 to 25 mph will
be accompanied by gusts of 25-35 mph. The higher range of the 
winds will be found across the foothills of the East Slopes, 
across the Waterville Plateau, and into the upper Columbia 
Basin. A second area of enhanced winds will channel along the 
Highway 12 corridor in the foothills of the Blue Mountains. 
There is a 65-75% chance for sustained winds of 20 mph or 
greater across the Waterville Plateau and Wilbur area and near 
40% at Pomeroy. There is a 80% chance for gusts to reach at 
least 30 mph in these areas and 35% chance for gusts to reach 40
mph. For much of North Idaho, Spokane Area, Moses Lake, and 
Omak gusts will be more on the order of 25-30 mph with sustained
speeds around 15 mph. Wind direction will start off from the 
west/southwest and shift toward the west/northwest into the 
afternoon into the evening. 

Little to no precipitation is expected with the incoming front 
east of the Cascade Crest. The Cascade crest will have a 90% 
chance for showers, some enhanced by the Puget Sound Convergence
zone but as precipitable water value tank late in the day, I 
expect these showers to wane by the evening. Snow levels on the 
Cascade Crest will be near 8000 feet, briefly dipping near 5000 
feet before showers taper off. 

Sunday-Wednesday: In the wake of Saturday's cold front, a shortwave 
ridge of high pressure will build over the region promoting 
lighter winds, sunny skies, and afternoon temperatures in the 
lower 60s. Another trough will approach the WA Coast Monday but 
a bulk of its energy will dig southward into California as a 
strong northerly jet develops on its backside. This will leave 
the Inland NW in the decaying northerly branch of a elongated 
trough. A trickle of moisture working its way into the region 
will introduce a 10-15% chance for showers but little in the way
of rainfall. Temperatures will not change much from Sunday 
through Tuesday cooling a degree or two and winds will shift 
around at light speeds from the east to south to north over the 
three day period. Overall, weather impacts are expected to be 
minimal. 

Thursday-Friday: There is strong support from the ensemble models 
for another trough to swing across the northern Pacific and 
through the PacNW. This will bring another bout of windy 
conditions and shot of cooler air in the region bringing the 
first potential for seasonal temperatures for the entire week 
(normal highs are in the 50s to low 60s). The incoming system 
will phase with the cutoff low over Northern California and has 
some potential to bring more shower activity into the region. 
Though, I am not convinced this will bring wetting rains (>0.10 
inches) as models seem to be trending drier and drier each 
consecutive run and only carry a 10-20% chance for a hundredth 
on the latest run. We'll have to see how this period evolves in 
the coming days. /sb
